{
  "summary": "Deprecates the `encryptwallet` RPC for encrypting existing unencrypted wallets, gating the command behind `-deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet` prior to future removal. Updates documentation and adapts functional tests across the test suite to create wallets encrypted upfront using `createwallet(passphrase=...)` instead of calling `encryptwallet` post-creation.",
  "problem": "Encrypting an existing wallet leaves plaintext key material behind on storage media (notably SSDs), creates a new seed that can invalidate pre-encryption backups and cause loss of funds, and silently alters spending conditions when manually imported descriptors are present.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description notes: 'Encrypting a wallet that has manually imported descriptors will cause the wallet to change the spending conditions out from under the user. (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/26607)'",
    "PR description notes: 'Because new keys are made after encryption, restoring from a backup made before encryption may result in loss of funds.'",
    "References open RFC #36027 ('[rfc] Remove encrypting wallets that already exist')."
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],
    "enables": [
      "#36027"
    ]
  },
  "scope_notes": "Most of the diff is mechanical test suite adjustments, either creating wallets with an initial passphrase via `createwallet` or adding `-deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet` to tests specifically covering `encryptwallet`.",
  "changed_since_previous": "Rebased or updated test refactors without changing the deprecation mechanism or PR scope.",
  "card": "Deprecates the encryptwallet RPC for encrypting existing unencrypted wallets, requiring -deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet ahead of eventual removal. Encrypting an unencrypted wallet risks fund loss because new keys generated upon encryption invalidate prior backups, unencrypted key fragments remain on disk, and wallets with imported descriptors can change spending conditions unexpectedly (issue 26607). Wallets can still be created encrypted from the start via createwallet. Functional tests across the suite are updated to initialize encrypted wallets directly.",
  "needs": [],
  "confidence": "high",
  "uncertainties": [],
  "risk": {
    "level": "medium",
    "touches": [
      "wallet",
      "rpc_api",
      "tests",
      "docs"
    ],
    "why": "Deprecating an existing RPC breaks external scripts or automated setups that rely on post-creation encryption unless -deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet is explicitly configured."
  }
}

result.summary: Deprecates the `encryptwallet` RPC for encrypting existing unencrypted wallets, gating the command behind `-deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet` prior to future removal. Updates documentation and adapts functional tests across the test suite to create wallets encrypted upfront using `createwallet(passphrase=...)` instead of calling `encryptwallet` post-creation.
result.problem: Encrypting an existing wallet leaves plaintext key material behind on storage media (notably SSDs), creates a new seed that can invalidate pre-encryption backups and cause loss of funds, and silently alters spending conditions when manually imported descriptors are present.
evidence: PR description notes: 'Encrypting a wallet that has manually imported descriptors will cause the wallet to change the spending conditions out from under the user. (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/26607)'
PR description notes: 'Because new keys are made after encryption, restoring from a backup made before encryption may result in loss of funds.'
References open RFC #36027 ('[rfc] Remove encrypting wallets that already exist').
result.scope_notes: Most of the diff is mechanical test suite adjustments, either creating wallets with an initial passphrase via `createwallet` or adding `-deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet` to tests specifically covering `encryptwallet`.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased or updated test refactors without changing the deprecation mechanism or PR scope.
result.card: Deprecates the encryptwallet RPC for encrypting existing unencrypted wallets, requiring -deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet ahead of eventual removal. Encrypting an unencrypted wallet risks fund loss because new keys generated upon encryption invalidate prior backups, unencrypted key fragments remain on disk, and wallets with imported descriptors can change spending conditions unexpectedly (issue 26607). Wallets can still be created encrypted from the start via createwallet. Functional tests across the suite are updated to initialize encrypted wallets directly.

risk.why: Deprecating an existing RPC breaks external scripts or automated setups that rely on post-creation encryption unless -deprecatedrpc=encryptwallet is explicitly configured.
